platforms.name: Browser extension (Chromium)
platforms.notes: The packaged zip strips the development key; the Chrome Web Store ID will differ from the unpacked ID. 1.5.2 adds one field to the native heartbeat: whether the browser lets the extension run in private/incognito windows (`chrome.extension.isAllowedIncognitoAccess`). The Mac app records it per browser and treats a false answer as an uncovered private-window gap; it never substitutes 'not allowed' when an older or silent browser gives no answer. 1.5.1's removal of the browser-side private-window mode and 1.5.0's portable rules and 1.4.0's quiet UI are retained.

platforms.name: Mac
platforms.state: development · unsigned, needs Developer ID and notarization
platforms.notes: Every target must carry the same MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION. 1.1.16 adds an aggregate blocked-connection count reported by the filter itself: a number for the current local day only, never a host, app or address, shown in the menu bar and the Overview's layer details. The app's authority request batch now continues past a dropped XPC reply instead of abandoning the rest until the next tick, and the menu bar shows the lock's coarse time remaining where it used to show the app name. 1.1.15's Organization Mode, 1.1.14's first-run/private-window pass and 1.1.13's private-windows profile are retained. Unsigned/unnotarized.

platforms.name: iPhone & iPad
platforms.state: development · no Apple team, Family Controls entitlement or test device
platforms.notes: The app, six Safari blockers, HisnActivityMonitor, the scanner and two shield extensions share one version set. 1.7.0 adds a pause rule: a fourth app-rule mode where the shield asks instead of only closing, a deliberately finished ten-second pause buys a session of chosen minutes, opens are limited per day, and a damaged budget record closes the day rather than guessing. The shield's Pause first action hands a request to Hisn — directly on iOS 26.5 and later, through a notification before that — the app grants in a failure-safe order, and the DeviceActivity monitor re-shields when the session ends. The editor adds opens per day and minutes per open. 1.6.0's browser/VPN guard and Lock Center, 1.5.0's card-stack overview, 1.4.0's bilingual shield, 1.3.0's pause, quiet hours and saved-rule freeze, and seed v5's core Safari list are retained. Simulator-tested only; real shielding and the shield's pause action need a signed, entitled device.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.state: development · 1.1.1 built and tested locally; no signed APK published
platforms.notes: versionCode is monotonic and must increase for every uploaded or side-loaded update. 27 (1.1.0) added the first-run welcome, the voluntary pause and today's usage in the daily-limit editor. 28 (1.1.1) lets the app schedule repeat on chosen weekdays: one window with a Monday-first day mask, every day by default for schedules saved before this version, an explicit day picker in the editor, and enforcement that keeps the overnight portion with the day the window starts on. The model and the accessibility service are the only enforcement; no permission, stored field or claim beyond the existing schedule is added. 1.0.0 added per-app daily foreground-time limits alongside the protection lock, removal guard, managed lockdown, watchdog and bundled-list warning. Release APKs are checked; the release keystore is in the gitignored keys/android and must be backed up offline in two places. The Play AAB is built but not uploaded.
